clue.text: Green record included by eastern company first

indicators.note: included by says the record sits inside the letters that the following words provide

parts.note: first is written 1ST, read here as IST
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: An environmental campaigner's record is endorsed by an eastern firm before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written as the ordinal 1ST, and the digit is read as the letter I; 'included by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A Green is a member of an environmental party, a person who studies or defends nature and habitats.

clue.text: Cautious with vehicle needing fuel adjustment

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: an adjustment rearranges things, so the letters of fuel are reordered

explanation.surface: A driver takes care when the car needs its fuel system tuned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment' is the anagram signal; 'needing' only links the vehicle to the fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a careful person is wary and takes pains to avoid danger.

clue.text: Bond, Alison I confused

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters of the name and pronoun are jumbled

explanation.surface: Alison is muddled about a bond she has formed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like the spy James Bond, but it is the definition; 'confused' rearranges ALISONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a close working connection or love affair is a tie between people.

clue.text: Provide information on the Queen at Exmouth

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the information is placed above what follows

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth
the mouth, or first letter, of the river Ex gives E

explanation.surface: Someone supplies details about Her Majesty's visit to the Devon town of Exmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' stacks GEN above ER in this down entry. Exmouth is a Devon seaside town; its 'mouth' here is the first letter of Ex.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to bring about or produce something, as a power station does electricity.

clue.text: Sounds like a real worker, but he's not there

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to say the phrase aloud and hear another word

parts.note: real is true, and a worker is an ant, the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A dedicated labourer is noticeably absent from his post.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE ANT said aloud gives a word for a pupil skipping school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who skips school is absent without leave, so he is missing from class.

clue.text: Fool that is leaving with a bronzed skin is a pretender

indicators.note: leaving means the words that is depart from the fool's name

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a tan is skin bronzed by the sun

explanation.surface: A suntanned clown who has walked away turns out to be a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes IE out of CHARLIE (British slang for a fool), leaving CHARL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a fraud who falsely claims skill or knowledge, a quack or impostor.

clue.text: Said in France, during another duel, to be a wrecker

indicators.note: during means the French word comes within the other letters
another duel is a different version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: dit is French for said

explanation.surface: A French remark made amid a second sword fight brands someone a saboteur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' signals the anagram of DUEL (a different version of the word), and 'during' the container; 'Said in France' points to French.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luddites were 19th-century workers who smashed machinery, so the word now means a saboteur of progress.

clue.text: Humble with our behaviour

parts.note: to humble someone is to demean them

explanation.surface: Being humble is part of how we conduct ourselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the way a person conducts and bears themselves, their manner.

clue.text: Provide new accommodation here, so could be posh inside

indicators.note: inside says the posh letter sits within the rearranged letters
could be signals that the letters of here and so can form something else

parts.note: U means upper-class, and so posh

explanation.surface: An estate agent suggests a smart home might be found right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges HERESO into REHOSE and 'inside' puts U (upper-class) in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehouse people is to move them to a fresh home.

clue.text: Consecrates on the other hand the said Scandinavians

parts.note: or introduces an alternative, as on the other hand does

indicators.note: the said asks us to hear the following word spoken

parts.note: Danes are Scandinavians from Denmark

explanation.surface: Alternatively, it is the Scandinavians who bless and sanctify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the said' turns DANES into the sound-alike DAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop who ordains a priest consecrates them to holy office.

clue.text: A game contract

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A card game in which players bid for a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a bridge bid, but it is the verb meaning shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to shorten a text or speech is to cut it down.

clue.text: Not employed as a film star?

definitions.text: Not employed as a film star?

parts.words: Not employed as a film star?
parts.note: a film star not working is literally away from the cinema screen, which also describes private life

explanation.definitionFit: Describes life away from the camera, as a performer out of work is not seen on film.

clue.text: Coarse grass in places part overgrown

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Rough grass has taken over some areas.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'places', all of 'part' and the start of 'overgrown'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough Spanish and North African grass used for paper and rope.

clue.text: Restrict development of train-set

indicators.note: development of means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Building a model railway is being limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' rearranges TRAINSET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to confine or limit, as in straitened circumstances.

clue.text: Design made by extraterrestrial of a heavenly body

parts.note: a plan is a design
ET is the abbreviation for extraterrestrial, from the film

explanation.surface: An alien draws up a blueprint of a star.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Mars or Jupiter is an orb orbiting a sun.

clue.text: Where entertainers are in their element in London?

definitions.text: Where entertainers are in their element in London?

parts.words: Where entertainers are in their element in London?
parts.note: names a famous London variety theatre, and also a metallic chemical element

explanation.walkthrough: The London Palladium is a famous West End theatre; palladium is also element 46.
explanation.definitionFit: A London variety venue that shares its name with a platinum-group metal.

clue.text: Disappear into thin air

parts.note: vanish, and literally turn into vapour in the atmosphere as water does

explanation.definitionFit: Liquid turning to vapour vanishes into the atmosphere, and things that vanish do likewise.

clue.text: Gallery found under cover and accessible in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An open gallery is sheltered and easy to reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed open porch along a house, like a gallery outside a building.

clue.text: Another tram damaged in the entrance to the park

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the entrance

parts.note: a door is an entrance

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of tram are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A second tram has been wrecked at the gates of a national park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' signals the anagram and 'in' the container. Dartmoor is a national park of moorland in Devon, southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a moorland national park in southwest England.

clue.text: Agitated lag in the morning repeatedly produces a soft mixture

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go within the other letters
repeatedly tells us to write the morning abbreviation twice

parts.note: AM is ante meridiem, the morning

indicators.note: agitated means shaken up, so the letters of lag are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stirred-up prisoner keeps making a paste each morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' signals the anagram, 'repeatedly' doubles the morning, and 'in' sets the shuffled prisoner (a lag is British slang for a convict) between.
explanation.definitionFit: An alloy of mercury and another metal, soft and used in dental fillings.

clue.text: One dropping a line left in a temper

indicators.note: in says the left letter goes inside the temper

parts.note: anger is a temper

explanation.surface: Someone hangs up the phone, departing in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping a line' sounds like ending a call or sending a note; it is casting a fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman casts a hook on a cord into the water.

clue.text: It is not difficult to spot this error

definitions.text: It is not difficult to spot this error

parts.words: It is not difficult to spot this error
parts.note: an obvious mistake is so conspicuous that anyone notices it

explanation.definitionFit: A blatant mistake stands out plainly, as such an error is called.

clue.text: Car tire?

definitions.meaning: the pipe at the back of a vehicle that carries away fumes

explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle's fume pipe, and a verb meaning to wear out or weary.

clue.text: Standard-bearer, one of many along the way

definitions.meaning: a lamp standard is a pole carrying a light, so it bears a standard

definitions.text: one of many along the way
definitions.meaning: street lights stand in rows along a road

explanation.definitionFit: A street-light pole, which carries a lamp and lines roads.

clue.text: Gets up and pays for everybody

definitions.meaning: to stand a round of drinks is to pay for the whole group

explanation.definitionFit: Rises to one's feet, and buys a round in a pub.

clue.text: Canine affliction?

parts.note: suggests a dog's illness but means pain in the pointed tooth beside the incisors

explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' suggests a dog, but a canine is also a pointed tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain in a tooth, here a canine one.

clue.text: Girl going round Rhode Island encounters frenzied conditions

indicators.note: going round says the girl's name encircles the state abbreviation

parts.note: Delia is a girl's name
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A girl touring an American state meets with wild scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' signals the container; Delia is just a girl's name, with no further clue to which one.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of a state of wild excitement or feverish confusion.

clue.text: Policeman, some say, with debts abounding

parts.note: cop is what some people, informally, call a policeman
IOUs are notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: An officer, people say, is overflowing with money owed.
explanation.walkthrough: IOU is short for 'I owe you', a written note of debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: plentiful, existing in great quantity.

clue.text: Not performed by one caught in the nude fidgeting

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Not performed by one caught in the nude fidgeting (7)': A (one) + C (caught) leaves UNTED, which 'the nude' (7 letters) cannot give by anagram; likely misprint for 'tuned', unconfirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Not performed by one caught in the nude fidgeting

clue.text: Deputy got us confused with rare concoction

indicators.note: confused means the letters of got us are jumbled
a concoction is a mix, so the letters of rare are stirred in too

explanation.surface: A stand-in has muddled us with some strange brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' and 'concoction' together rearrange GOTUS and RARE as one pool of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a substitute acting in another's place.
